blocks.content: These two instructions both define what runs when a container starts, and they are the single most confused pair in Docker. The clean way to think about it: ENTRYPOINT is the fixed program, CMD is its default arguments.

Anything typed after the image name on docker run replaces CMD completely. That same text does not replace ENTRYPOINT at all, it gets appended as arguments to it instead, unless you use the explicit --entrypoint flag.

blocks.alt: ENTRYPOINT is fixed, CMD is a replaceable default

blocks.content: Seeing what actually happens on override makes the distinction concrete: extra arguments append onto ENTRYPOINT, but they entirely replace a plain CMD.

blocks.alt: Append versus replace, the whole difference in one picture

blocks.content: {"headers":["","CMD","ENTRYPOINT"],"rows":[["docker run img extra-arg behavior","Replaces CMD entirely","Appends extra-arg to ENTRYPOINT"],["How to force a full override","Just pass a new command","Requires the --entrypoint flag"],["Best used for","A default command, meant to be swappable","A fixed purpose, the container IS this program"]]}
Used together, ENTRYPOINT fixes the binary while CMD supplies default arguments to it, giving you a container with a stable identity but a still-overridable default behavior.

blocks.alt: A fixed program, with overridable default arguments

blocks.content:
ENTRYPOINT ["python", "app.py"]
CMD ["--port=8000"]

# docker run myimage                 -> python app.py --port=8000
# docker run myimage --port=9000     -> python app.py --port=9000

code.content:

CMD ["--port=8000"]

# docker run myimage                 -> python app.py --port=8000
# docker run myimage --port=9000     -> python app.py --port=9000

codes.dockerfile:
ENTRYPOINT ["python", "app.py"]
CMD ["--port=8000"]

# docker run myimage                 -> python app.py --port=8000
# docker run myimage --port=9000     -> python app.py --port=9000

blocks.content: If a container should behave like a general tool with a sensible default (easily replaced entirely), lean on CMD alone. If a container has one fixed purpose, and you want to guarantee it always runs that program no matter what arguments someone passes, use ENTRYPOINT, with CMD supplying just the default arguments.

blocks.alt: A flexible default versus a guaranteed, fixed behavior

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: ENTRYPOINT is a fixed program that extra arguments get appended to, CMD is a fully replaceable default command.
Combining them, ENTRYPOINT for the fixed binary, CMD for its default arguments, is a common and powerful pattern.
